This Collection supports and amplifies research related to SDG 2 and SDG 12 and SDG 13.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is opening new opportunities to understand plant traits and responses, monitor plant health and support more resilient and sustainable production. Advances in machine learning, computer vision, sensing and robotics can connect biological observations with predictive models and practical decision-making across laboratory, greenhouse and field environments. However, translating these capabilities into reliable scientific and agricultural outcomes requires approaches that account for biological variability, heterogeneous data, limited annotations and changing environmental conditions. Close collaboration between plant scientists and AI researchers is therefore essential to develop methods that are relevant to plant science and robust beyond individual experimental settings.

This Collection brings together interdisciplinary research on AI for the study, monitoring, improvement and management of plants. It spans the pathway from fundamental plant understanding to sustainable production, welcoming both advances in AI methodologies and the use of established methods to address important biological and agronomic questions. Contributions may provide scientific insights, improved analytical capabilities, enabling datasets and technologies, or validated applications in plant research and production.

We also encourage datasets, benchmarks and digital research infrastructure that enable reproducible research, support evaluation across species, cultivars, locations and seasons, and facilitate collaboration between plant science and AI communities. Studies addressing generalisation, interpretability and robustness are welcome across all areas of the Collection.

Across these areas, contributions should demonstrate clear relevance to plant science and provide validation appropriate to their research questions and intended use. Scientific discovery, improved measurement and prediction, and reliable tools for plant production are complementary contributions. Studies may focus on particular species or settings, or investigate approaches designed for wider transfer and deployment. By bringing together complementary perspectives, this Collection aims to strengthen the links between AI development and plant research, highlighting how these technologies can support discovery, healthier and more resilient crops, and more efficient and sustainable production.
